date:jerusalem-council@f5067f.note: No year in the text. It gives only the order: the dispute, then the apostles and elders meet at Jerusalem. AD 46 depends on outside chronology.

date:mission-to-antioch-in-pisidia@d50e3.note: No year in the text. It places the mission after Perga, on the way to Antioch in Pisidia. AD 45 depends on outside chronology.

date:mission-to-iconium@f5067f.note: No year in the text. It says only that they went into the synagogue at Iconium. AD 46 depends on outside chronology.

date:mission-to-lystra-and-derbe@f5067f.note: No year in the text. It says they fled to Lystra and Derbe after Iconium. AD 46 depends on outside chronology.

date:paul-and-barnabas-part-ways@a4e617.note: No year in the text. It gives only the sequence: the proposed revisit, then the sharp contention. AD 47 depends on outside chronology.

date:return-to-antioch-in-syria@f5067f.note: No year in the text. It gives only the order: the return through the cities, then sailing back to Antioch. AD 46 depends on outside chronology.

date:second-missionary-journey@b74492.note: No year in the text. It gives only the sequence from the revisit plan to going through Syria and Cilicia. AD 46 to 49 depends on outside chronology.

occurred-at:barnabas-and-saul-go-to-cypr.note: They departed to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus. The text starts the trip at Seleucia but does not place the event there.

occurred-at:first-missionary-journey>ant.note: The automatic match cited 13.1, which is Antioch in Syria. 13:14 says they came to Antioch in Pisidia during the journey.

occurred-at:first-missionary-journey>sel.note: They departed unto Seleucia to sail for Cyprus. Seleucia is the starting port of the trip, not a stop the journey is described at.

occurred-at:mission-to-antioch-in-pisidi.note: They were expelled from Antioch, then went on to Iconium. That is a later stop on the route, not the place where this mission happened.
13:13 says only John returned to Jerusalem. Paul and his company went on to Antioch in Pisidia (13:14).
Pamphylia (Perga) is a stop before Antioch in Pisidia (13:13-14), on the route, not where the mission was held.
Paphos is left before the journey to Antioch in Pisidia (13:13-14). It is a stop on the route, not the mission site.
Perga is reached before Antioch in Pisidia (13:13-14). It is a stop on the route, not the mission site.

occurred-at:paul-and-barnabas-part-ways>.note: They were in Antioch (15:35) when the contention arose. Barnabas sailed to Cyprus only after they separated (15:39).

occurred-at:return-to-antioch-in-syria>a.note: 14:21 lists Antioch among the cities revisited on the way back. Antioch in Pisidia is on the return route, not the Syrian return point.
They went down to Attalia on the return, then sailed to Antioch (14:25-26). A stop on the route, not the Syrian Antioch.

occurred-at:return-to-antioch-in-syria>i.note: On the way back they returned to Iconium (14:21). A stop on the route before Antioch, not the place of the return.

occurred-at:return-to-antioch-in-syria>l.note: On the way back they returned to Lystra (14:21). A stop on the route before Antioch, not the place of the return.

occurred-at:return-to-antioch-in-syria>p.note: They came to Pamphylia on the return (14:24). A stop on the route, not the place of the return to Antioch.
They preached in Perga on the return (14:25). A stop on the route, not the place of the return to Antioch.
They passed throughout Pisidia on the return (14:24). A stop on the route, not the place of the return to Antioch.

occurred-at:second-missionary-journey-be.note: They were at Antioch (15:35), and Paul chose Silas and departed (15:40). Antioch is implied as the start, but the text does not name it.
15:41 says Paul went through Syria and Cilicia after leaving. Cilicia is a stop on the route, not the start.
Antioch lies in Syria, and 15:41 has them going through Syria. The text names the region along the route, not a starting point.

part-of:attalia_120>pamphylia_918@10aeb9.note: 14:24-25 gives Pamphylia, then Perga and Attalia in order. That Attalia lies within Pamphylia is plausible but not stated.

part-of:paphos_919>cyprus_316@fb667e.note: They sailed to Cyprus, then went through 'the isle' to Paphos (13:4, 13:6). The text does not name the island, but the isle is Cyprus.

part-of:salamis_1016>cyprus_316@886ad3.note: They sailed to Cyprus and were at Salamis (13:4-5). The text does not say Salamis is on the island, though it is.
